title: Line classes, generator extensions and normalized cohomology transport on ringed sites
statement: For a site $(C,J)$ small relative to the sheaf universe [def-weil-size-convention] [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and a commutative ring sheaf $A$, put $A^\times(U)=A(U)^\times$ additively, and let $\operatorname{Line}(A)$ be the module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] locally free of rank one. Put $\operatorname{Pic}(A)=\operatorname{Line}(A)/\cong$. A frame over $U$ is a section whose scalar-multiplication map is bijective on every $V\to U$; equivalently it is $A|_U\cong M|_U$. A generator-torsor presentation is a units torsor whose sections identify with these frames compatibly with restriction and multiplication by units. A generator extension is a short exact sequence $0\to A^\times\to E\to\mathbf Z\to0$ with the fibre over $1$ identified with the frames, compatibly with restriction and translation by units. A Picard-comparison presentation consists of an abelian group law on the actual quotient whose zero is the unit line and whose addition is the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], together with an additive equivalence to $H^1(C,A^\times)$ normalized on each line by the class of every generator extension, and existence of the generator torsors and extensions. For a ringed-topos morphism [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] with independent site universes [def-pur-ringed-topos-morphism-of-universes], a cohomology transport is an abelian inverse-image presentation [def-trf-abelian-inverse-image-presentation] which is additive and exact, with its integer-sheaf comparison preserving the global section $1$. Pullback on $H^n=\operatorname{Ext}^n(\mathbf Z,-)$ is exact-functor transport followed by precomposition with this comparison. Its resolution-computation predicate says that for any specified coefficient sheaf and every pair of injective resolutions a comparison $\beta$ under inverse image exists, and every degree-one global cocycle $a:\mathbf Z\to I^1$ is sent to $\mathbf Z\to f^{-1}\mathbf Z\xrightarrow{f^{-1}a}f^{-1}I^1\xrightarrow{\beta^1}J^1$. A coefficient map on units is structural if its underlying value map is the inverse image of unit inclusion followed by the structural ring map. Algebraic inverse images used in tensor pullback retain their transported ring and module operations [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image].
